changes.before: Remove drop=FALSE. What class prints for this numeric column?
changes.after: Selecting just one column can turn a data frame into a vector.

before: Selecting one data-frame column with frame[, "score"] normally simplifies to the underlying vector.
frame[, "score", drop=FALSE] keeps a one-column data frame. The values are the same, but the container shape differs.

A function expecting row/column structure can behave differently when given a vector. Do not infer shape only from the printed numbers.

class(selected) receives the selected object and returns its class label here. The displayed data.frame result confirms the retained container class; it is not a value from the score column.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
frame <- data.frame(score=c(2, 4))
selected <- frame[, "score", drop=FALSE]
cat(class(selected))
```
Expected output or behavior: data.frame. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
